message.text: Checking connect.ts to identify the auth interceptor and how refresh tokens are stored—cookie versus localStorage—to name the token kinds accurately.

The frontend auth interceptor lives in `web/src/connect.ts`. It manages access tokens (Bearer JWTs stored in localStorage) and refresh tokens (via a RefreshToken RPC call with credentials included, using cookies). The backend package that validates these tokens is still being identified.

The backend package is `server/auth`, which contains the `Authenticator` used by `NewAuthInterceptor` in `connect_interceptors.go` via an `Authorizer`.

q29.
web/src/connect.ts; access JWT (Bearer) and refresh token (cookie); server/auth

The Connect `authInterceptor` in `web/src/connect.ts` attaches `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` from `web/src/auth-state.ts` (localStorage) and, on expiry or 401, calls `RefreshToken` with `credentials: "include"` so the refresh cookie is sent. The backend validates those tokens in `server/auth` (`Authenticator` in `authenticator.go`); Connect wiring is `NewAuthInterceptor` in `server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`. PATs are also accepted by the authenticator but are not what the frontend interceptor issues.
